status: exploratory follow-up of E13 (decides no registered E13 prediction); written after the E13 result and the E13c diagnostic, before any S6/S7 run
motivation: E13 (qwen0.5b, 3 seeds): the all-on swarm with K=2 of 4 and a persistent straggler on one non-IID domain keeps -0.05 +- 0.35 of the synchronous improvement (P13b refuted), K=M keeps 0.94, and rotating the straggler (E13c) recovers 0.40 +- 0.30: starvation of one domain explains part of it, K<M itself the rest.

mechanisms.S6_fair_quorum: bounded exclusion: an alive worker excluded from MAX_EXCLUSION=1 consecutive closed rounds must be in the next quorum; the round closes only after K-quorum + grace AND every such worker has posted (that delta is then admitted); dead workers never block; the extra wait is capped at 0.5 x the stall-watchdog limit (900 s in round 1), after which the round closes with what is there (fair_wait_timeouts recorded); counters reset on admission and on a new incarnation
mechanisms.S7_deferred_carry: a late or outside-grace delta is queued instead of discarded and merged into the NEXT round as an extra arrival (merge mode of the cell: RDA) with weight token_weight / (1 + s), s = current version - base version; deltas with s > MAX_STALENESS=2 are discarded and counted; dead or stale-incarnation posts are rejected at arrival; carried deltas do not count toward K or the grace window
mechanisms.both: identical to S2 otherwise: K=ceil(M/2), adaptive grace, RDA, E8@2+EF, the registered straggler (worker M-1 delayed 2x in rounds 1,3,5) and churn (worker 1 killed after round 2, re-spawned before round 4)

granite1b.note: pretrained MoE (32 experts, top-8); the first MoE test of the fairness mechanisms

grid.rounds_inner_optimizer_data_heldout: exactly as E13 (6 rounds x 20 inner steps, micro-batch 4 x 256, PEFT-scale LoRA init, stride-sampled held-out sequences per domain)
grid.S2_note: S2 is re-run in the same invocation so that S2, S6 and S7 are paired seed by seed under identical code; it also replicates the registered E13 S2 retention (scheduling nondeterminism differs between runs and is reported)

hypotheses_and_rules.H14a: S6 keeps more of the synchronous improvement than S2: per-seed paired difference loss(S2) - loss(S6); df=2 95% t-interval (t = 4.302652729911275); supported if the interval is above 0, refuted if it is below 0, inconclusive if it includes 0
hypotheses_and_rules.H14c_descriptive: registered retention rho = (L_round0 - L_cell)/(L_round0 - L_S0) per seed for S2, S6, S7 against the 0.5 viability bar of P13b and the K=M value (0.94 on qwen0.5b in E13); round-latency increase of S6, carried deltas / staleness histogram of S7, upload bytes
hypotheses_and_rules.no_multiple_comparison_correction: two hypotheses per model, stated as exploratory

controls: S0 learns (final < initial); S0 twin bit-identical; no failed cells; mean measured codec rate within 0.05 of 2.0 bit/dim; hosting recorded; the registered fail-fast gates (learning 0.05 nats at round 3, --max-hours 3.0) apply
decision_consequences: H14a and/or H14b supported on a model: the mechanism is a candidate admission policy for the multi-host gameday (HM-S9-07) and a new roadmap item (HM-S10-09), to be confirmed with more seeds and on the WAN; both refuted: the quorum problem needs data leasing (HM-S9-06) or K=M with a longer grace; this experiment cannot change the E13 verdicts
scope: one GPU, thread-hosted peers, 3 seeds, 2 models, 6 rounds; no WAN claim; fixed constants (MAX_EXCLUSION 1, MAX_STALENESS 2) not tuned
sizing: qwen0.5b: 13 runs (including the S0b twin) of 480 inner steps at about 0.3 s/step, about 1 h; granite1b: 13 runs of 360 steps at about 1.1 s/step, about 1.4 h
